note: Written cold from decomposePrompt without sight of the validator — the closest thing here to real model output. Negotiation turned the unscopeable "AI" into a bounded goal in two turns.

goal.statement: Trace a single token through a small transformer and say what each stage does to it, and why attention is the part that makes it work.
goal.audience: a programmer with no machine learning background

capstone.prompt: Take the sentence "the cat sat on the" and walk through what happens to the word "cat" from input to the model's prediction of the next word. Say what attention contributes that a plain feed-forward network could not.
rubric: follows the token as a vector through each stage
explains attention as weighted mixing of other positions
names what is learned versus what is computed
does not treat the model as a lookup table

kcs.label: A transformer processes input tokens in stages: embedding, self-attention, feed-forward, and output.
misconceptions: Transformers operate like traditional recurrent neural networks.
Self-attention only focuses on nearby words.
Feed-forward networks alone can capture long-range dependencies between words.

check.stem: What happens during the self-attention stage of a transformer?
options: It only considers the last word.
It replaces the input sequence with random values.
distractorSource: Transformers operate like traditional recurrent neural networks.
Self-attention only focuses on nearby words.
Feed-forward networks alone can capture long-range dependencies between words.

kcs.label: Self-attention computes a weighted representation of input tokens based on their relationships.
misconceptions: Self-attention gives equal importance to all words.
Attention weights are static and do not change during training.

check.stem: What does self-attention do with the input tokens?
options: It assigns equal weights to all tokens.
It operates at a fixed layer only.
distractorSource: Self-attention gives equal importance to all words.
Attention weights are static and do not change during training.

kcs.label: Attention enables the model to focus on relevant parts of the input sequence based on the target token's context.
misconceptions: Attention works the same as simple aggregation of inputs.
The mechanism only benefits long inputs.
It cannot replace other neural network types.

check.stem: Why is attention significant in transformers?
distractorSource: Attention works the same as simple aggregation of inputs.
The mechanism only benefits long inputs.
It cannot replace other neural network types.

kcs.label: Each stage (embedding, self-attention, feed-forward) transforms the token representation to maintain or enhance semantic meaning.
misconceptions: Transformations do not change token meaning.
Only the output layer matters for predictions.
Pre-trained models do not utilize embeddings effectively.

check.stem: What is the purpose of transformations in a transformer?
options: To compress all input to a single value.
To eliminate the need for context.
distractorSource: Transformations do not change token meaning.
Only the output layer matters for predictions.
Pre-trained models do not utilize embeddings effectively.
